answer: Every agent identity must lock a small non-refundable stake that drains each day at dawn while the identity stays active, and the stake can only be refilled from a shared oasis of fees earned by completed, verified work. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities pays the stake for every fake and keeps paying the daily drain, so forgery costs scale linearly with the number of fakes; honest agents recover their stake from real earnings, growing steadily like yarrow in poor soil while the attacker's budget withers before it ever scales.
